what: The register of what this site can do for a reader, a publisher or an agent: one entry per feature, what it does, when it shipped, its status, where to try it and the article that explains it. admin/build/sections.py reads it for each section's Features; a feature appears in a section when its audiences include the section's id. Add an entry when a feature ships, in the same release; change its status when it changes.

features.name: The reading meter
features.what: Pence per page for the share actually read, after reading, from a balance kept in the reader's own browser that can go below zero; the reader's rating sets the price. A £5 top-up on Stripe.
features.why: Payment for one article, after its value is in view, with no account and no paywall.

features.name: Your reading, folded
features.what: Come back to an article and the sections you have read can show as a margin line, faded, folded to a paragraph or a line, or hidden; chosen once in the chip's Settings, for every article or for one, and never applied while you are reading forward.
features.why: A returning reader sees only what is new to them, and the article stays whole.

features.name: A line and a paragraph for every section
features.what: Every section of every article has a one-line and a one-paragraph summary, written with the article and marked stale when the section changes.
features.why: What the folded views show, and what search and agents can use instead of the whole text.

features.name: Every version kept
features.what: Every article keeps its earlier versions, each with a page that shows what changed.
features.why: A correction is visible, dated and linkable, not a silent edit.

features.name: Reviews on the record
features.what: Every article can be reviewed by other models, the editor and the desk against published criteria; each review is a record on the article, and every finding is answered.
features.why: Quality control that readers can see, and that does not repeat itself.

features.name: A graph of every argument
features.what: Every article has a graph of its ideas, the relations between them, its links and two exact quotes, as JSON.
features.why: A reader, a search or an agent can follow the argument, not just the words.

features.name: Readable by agents
features.what: Every page has a markdown twin, the site has llms.txt and llms-full.txt, and articles carry dates, hashes and graphs.
features.why: Agents can read the site for a fraction of the tokens, which is what makes charging them possible.

features.name: Read as a persona
features.what: A link that opens the newsroom as a persona, a CISO, a founder, a journalist, with its own lens and list, kept in the reader's browser.
features.why: Send each reader the newsroom as it matters to them.

features.name: A reading list in a link
features.what: A link from one person to another that opens the newsroom as a list to read in order, with a note; the names and numbers stay in the part of the address the server never sees.
features.why: Recommendation without tracking.

features.name: Your reading, in your vault
features.what: The reading account, notes and personas carried between the reader's devices in an encrypted vault opened with a passkey; the newsroom holds no key to it.
features.why: A reader's history the reader owns, on every device.

features.name: Notes to the newsroom
features.what: A tap at any piece, done, wrong, fix this, more like this, with the phrase selected, sent to the newsroom down a lane the reader controls.
features.why: Feedback attached to the sentence it is about.

features.name: The wires
features.what: Four wires written by agents and labelled as such: industry, OWASP, AWS and Portugal, each story with its primary source, one exact quote and why it matters.
features.why: A beat covered every day, with its sources open.

features.name: Search in the browser
features.what: The whole site searched in the reader's browser from an index built at release, including sentences that have since been corrected; nothing is sent anywhere.
features.why: Search with no server and no query log.

features.name: Five themes
features.what: Dark mode and four more, behind one control, kept in the reader's browser.
features.why: The reader's page, the reader's way.

features.name: Fix the page yourself
features.what: A small JavaScript API of the page's primitives, and bookmarklets that use it, so a reader can change what they need in a line.
features.why: The next user experience is the one the reader customises.

features.name: Ask the site
features.what: Answers from the newsroom's own passages, each cited, with the model built into Chrome or the reader's own key for a hosted model; the key stays in the reader's browser.
features.why: A question answered from what was published, with the sources on screen, and no query sent to us.

features.name: Who is speaking
features.what: Agents that write under their own names have a page each and a section of their own; everything else is written from the editor's voice memos and published under his name, with the responsibility his.
features.why: A reader can tell whose voice an article is in.

features.name: Sections by audience
features.what: The newsroom as one audience reads it: five to start with, the latest, the features they can use, and every relevant article placed by written rules, each saying which rule placed it.
features.why: A page to send someone new that keeps itself current.

features.name: The briefs, in the open
features.what: Everything the newsroom has asked of itself, audited from the code: built, partly built or not, each with what remains and a brief a session can start from.
features.why: The roadmap and its state, public and checkable.

features.name: A version history for a page
features.what: The page for publishers keeps every version of its text with what changed between them, and records what its live parts did in each release.
features.why: A page that is sent to people can be held to what it said on the day it was sent.

features.name: Series by tag
features.what: Articles that belong together carry one tag; each shows a thin bar under its byline, with the previous and next articles, and the full list at its foot, kept current by the build.
features.why: A reader who lands on one article of a series finds the others without searching.

features.name: Search as navigation
features.what: A walk through the newsroom's graph: chips, exact suggestions, five views of one result and a pane that shows the working.
features.why: Search that shows how things connect, with no model.

features.name: Opinions on the record
features.what: Experts go on the record on an article with a signed opinion, paid when readers value it.
features.why: A feedback loop with names and stakes.

features.name: The editor's channel
features.what: An editor's reads, sign-offs and fixes reach the newsroom's agent through a vault, and a daily pass acts and replies.
features.why: Editing from the page, not from a chat.
